questions.q: Why does Lesson 47's truncate-and-reload approach not scale?
options: Every run re-extracts the entire source table, even orders loaded in previous runs, getting slower as the source grows
SSIS packages can only run a fixed number of times before failing
AdventureWorks2012 deletes old orders automatically
Truncate statements are not supported by SQL Server
questions.explain: A full reload re-does the same work on every run regardless of what actually changed, which is fine on a small lab table but becomes a real problem as the source table grows.

questions.q: What does the watermark (CapstoneLoadControl.LastLoadDate) get used for?
options: Filtering the source query to only rows modified after the last successful run
Storing the package's password
Counting how many times the package has ever been deployed
Replacing the need for a Data Flow Task entirely
questions.explain: The source query's WHERE clause filters on ModifiedDate > the stored watermark, so each run only extracts what's new or changed since the last successful load.

questions.q: What does changing the Lookup transformation's error output to Redirect Row accomplish?
options: Rows that don't match CapstoneDimProduct get routed to a separate output (here, a flat file) instead of being silently dropped
It makes the Lookup match every row automatically, regardless of ProductID
It disables the Lookup transformation entirely
It causes the whole package to fail immediately on any unmatched row
questions.explain: Redirect Row sends failing rows down a separate error path — here, into capstone_lookup_errors.csv — so unmatched rows are captured and visible instead of vanishing.

questions.q: What does the OnError event handler on the Data Flow Task do?
options: Inserts a row into a custom log table recording the failure, even if no one is watching the package run
Automatically fixes whatever error occurred
Prevents the Data Flow Task from ever failing again
Emails the package's source code to the administrator
questions.explain: An OnError event handler runs package logic in response to a failure — here, writing a record to dbo.CapstoneRunLog so the failure leaves a trace.

questions.q: After adding the watermark, what should happen if you run the package twice in a row with no new orders added in between?
options: The second run loads zero rows, since nothing has changed since the first run's watermark
The second run reloads every row again, exactly like the first run
The second run deletes everything the first run loaded
The package refuses to run a second time at all
questions.explain: With the source query filtering on ModifiedDate > the stored watermark and no new or changed orders in between, the second run correctly finds nothing new to extract.
